steps.tx: The International League Against Epilepsy categorises seizures into focal, generalised, and unknown onset based on initial electroclinical manifestations. A classic primary **generalised tonic-clonic seizure** begins abruptly with loss of consciousness, sustained bilateral axial muscle rigidity (tonic phase) accompanied by an ictal cry, transitioning after thirty seconds into rhythmic, synchronous muscular contractions (clonic phase) with tongue biting and urinary incontinence.
steps.say: The International League Against Epilepsy categorises seizures into focal, generalized, and unknown onset. A generalized tonic-clonic seizure begins abruptly with loss of consciousness, sustained muscular rigidity during the tonic phase, transitioning into rhythmic synchronous contractions during the clonic phase with tongue biting and incontinence.

steps.tx: A non-motor generalised seizure occurring predominantly in school-aged children is the typical **absence seizure** (petit mal). Characterised by sudden, brief lapses of consciousness lasting five to ten seconds with an unblinking glassy stare and immediate resumption of previous activity without postictal confusion, episodes can be reliably provoked during clinical examination by hyperventilation.
steps.say: A non-motor generalized seizure occurring predominantly in school-aged children is the typical absence seizure. Characterized by sudden brief lapses of consciousness lasting five to ten seconds with an unblinking stare and immediate recovery without confusion, attacks are readily provoked by hyperventilation.

left.title: Typical Absence Seizure
points: Absence of postictal drowsiness or confusion

right.title: Focal Impaired Awareness Seizure
points: Preceded by autonomic or psychic aura

steps.tx: The pathognomonic electroencephalographic hallmark of typical absence epilepsy is generalised, symmetrical, synchronous **3 Hz spike and wave** discharges. Generated by abnormal oscillatory resonance within thalamocortical relay circuits involving low-threshold T-type voltage-gated calcium channels, first-line therapeutic control is achieved with ethosuximide or sodium valproate.
steps.say: The pathognomonic electroencephalographic hallmark of typical absence epilepsy is generalized symmetrical synchronous 3 Hz spike and wave discharges. Generated by abnormal oscillatory resonance within thalamocortical relay circuits involving T-type calcium channels, first-line control is achieved with ethosuximide.

steps.tx: In contrast to generalised seizures, a **focal seizure** originates within neuronal networks limited to one cerebral hemisphere. Focal aware seizures preserve consciousness (such as motor twitching of a hand or sensory paraesthesias), whereas focal impaired awareness seizures (formerly complex partial seizures) compromise consciousness, typically feature oroalimentary automatisms (lip smacking, swallowing), and localise to the temporal lobe.
steps.say: In contrast to generalized seizures, a focal seizure originates within neuronal networks limited to one cerebral hemisphere. Focal aware seizures preserve consciousness, whereas focal impaired awareness seizures compromise awareness, feature oroalimentary automatisms, and typically localise to the temporal lobe.

rows: Focal motor clonic jerking (Jacksonian march) or sensory tingling
Emanates from mesial temporal sclerosis; automatisms common
Glassy stare, 3 Hz spike-wave, no postictal lethargy
Shock-like morning jerks of upper limbs in JME

steps.tx: An idiopathic generalised epilepsy syndrome presenting in adolescence with characteristic morning bilateral shock-like arrhythmic jerks is **juvenile myoclonic epilepsy** (JME, Janz syndrome). Triggered by sleep deprivation and photic stimulation, patients experience myoclonic jerks (dropping cups in the morning), generalised tonic-clonic seizures, and absence seizures, responding exquisitely to life-long sodium valproate.
steps.say: An idiopathic generalized epilepsy syndrome presenting in adolescence with morning bilateral shock-like jerks is juvenile myoclonic epilepsy. Triggered by sleep deprivation and flashing lights, patients experience myoclonic jerks, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and absence seizures, responding well to sodium valproate.

steps.tx: An infantile epileptic encephalopathy presenting in the first year of life with flexion spasms, developmental regression, and chaotic hypsarrhythmia on electroencephalography is **West syndrome**. The classic triad of infantile spasms, arrest of psychomotor development, and hypsarrhythmia responds first-line to adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) or vigabatrin (specifically indicated in tuberous sclerosis).
steps.say: An infantile epileptic encephalopathy presenting in the first year of life with flexion spasms, developmental regression, and chaotic hypsarrhythmia on EEG is West syndrome. The triad of infantile spasms, developmental arrest, and hypsarrhythmia responds to adrenocorticotropic hormone or vigabatrin.

right.title: Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome
points: Onset 2 to 7 years (often evolves from West)
Multiple seizure types (atonic, tonic, atypical absence)
Severe intellectual disability and drug resistance

steps.tx: Evolution into childhood often gives rise to **Lennox-Gastaut syndrome**, a devastating epileptic encephalopathy characterised by a triad of multiple polymorphic seizure types (especially atonic drop attacks and nocturnal tonic seizures), severe cognitive impairment, and an interictal EEG displaying slow spike-and-wave discharges under 2.5 Hz.
steps.say: Evolution into childhood often gives rise to Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, a severe epileptic encephalopathy characterized by multiple polymorphic seizure types, atonic drop attacks, severe cognitive impairment, and an EEG displaying slow spike-and-wave discharges under 2.5 Hz.

steps.tx: A critical neurological emergency defined as continuous seizure activity lasting five minutes or longer, or recurrent seizures without full neurological recovery between episodes, is **status epilepticus**. Prolonged sustained seizure discharges exhaust neuronal glucose stores, induce excitotoxic NMDA glutamate receptor overactivation, and cause systemic hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, and irreversible hippocampal neuronal necrosis.
steps.say: A critical neurological emergency defined as continuous seizure activity lasting five minutes or longer, or recurrent seizures without recovery between attacks, is status epilepticus. Sustained seizure discharges exhaust neuronal glucose stores, induce glutamate excitotoxicity, and cause irreversible hippocampal neuronal necrosis.
